item.content:encoded:
That makes complete sense - we're actually watching the safe-for-human version of the logs (I actually feel kind of dumb for not thinking about that before…).

As for the "many plot holes" you refer to, while I did notice a few other things (for example, Qasim's exosuit being out of range of Manu, but then when Kumaran and Pang get to that location later, they're still within range), really, this is inevitable in a text of this complexity; and seeing as all of them were very minor and had no real impact on the plot (which would mean they're not even technically plot holes), I think you're good. :)

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Whew, the first of many plot holes comes to light :p

I imagine that the raw video feed was sent to Overwatch HQ, and parsed under the same filtering software to get something human-viewable for the transcript.

And thank you for liking the Manu/mysterious entity interactions, I had a lot of fun writing those!

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This is simply terrific, easily one of the best single entries in the contest.

Sure, it's incredibly long, but it's so engrossing that time just flies. The conversations between Manu and the entity were also fascinating and eerie and tense, and the high point of the article for me, even if it was fairly obvious what there were leading to (not that guessing the twist affected my enjoyment of the story in any way, mind you). The hidden text was also neat, and not at all gimmicky.

I just have one technical question: why were the video feeds from the exo-suits to the landers scrambled? Wouldn't it be possible to scramble the image on the viewscreens inside the suits, while leaving the video feed itself uncensored? I just ask because it seems like it would be useful to have the cognito-hazards on record for study, even if they can only be examined by AIs.

+10, well done.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: This is the best AAR entry in the contest. It is the climax of the Rho-19 story, told with rising tension, and using the epistolary documentary style of the piece to limit the information available to the reader, but without being confusing or breaking immersion.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I'm inordinately proud of it

You absolutely should be, minmin. I remember you saying on chat that you were worried about the degree of difficulty here - laying out a climax, building on what had come before (including the anticipation built up by some very good entries from your team) and staying true to the characters.

You have succeeded in pulling all of that off. This was an appropriately epic descent into the mind of the maze, and into the question of what humanity is. I am really looking forward to reading the discussion of this tale for a long time to come.

item.content:encoded:
This is a lot of things. It's a descent into quasi-religious mania, an alien consciousness communicating with another almost-alien consciousness, a debate on what it means to be alive, an exploration of a temple of doom, and an ending that leaves one with a lot to ponder.

It's also damn good.
